newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH COAL TRADER WEGLOKOKS EYES SALE IN Q2 97.
newsitem.headline: POLISH COAL TRADER WEGLOKOKS EYES SALE IN Q2 97.

text.p: Poland's biggest coal and coke trader Weglokoks SA is likely to be privatised by the end of the second quarter of 1997, a Weglokoks deputy president said on Thursday.

Jozef Wolski told a news conference the treasury could sell up to 45 percent of shares to institutional investors, both financial and strategic, and place 15 to 30 percent on the Warsaw Stock Exchange.
It is also likely to offer 15 percent of shares to employees and keep five percent for reprivatisations claims.
"In December the government will decide on the way Weglokoks will be privatised," Wolski said.

Last month the industry ministry picked a consortium of the Polish Development Bank (PBR) , the cooperative Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej SA (BGZ), consultants Business Management and Finance SA (BM&F) and auditors Potworowski Kinast Grant Thornton.
Head of BM&F Wojciech Janczyk, also present, said the exact division of shares between tranches and their price would be decided next year by the advising consortium.

Within the consortium BM&F is to prepare the general strategy for the offering, PBR is to provide legal support to seek investors, Potworowski will do the firm's audit and BGZ is to prepare the issue prospectus and lead the public offering.
PBR and BGZ might also underwrite the public issue.

A Weglokoks official, who asked not to be named, said many of the banks which held Weglokoks accounts -- Bank Handlowy, Citibank, Bank Slaski , BRE , BGZ and Bank Ochrony Srodowiska -- were interested in taking a stake in the firm.

BM&F's Janczyk also said that the company was in talks with its foreign partners and financial institutions, such as the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, on their potential participation in the privatisation.

Weglokoks had a net profit of 25.3 million zlotys in the first 10 months of this year against just under a million in the same period of 1995 on sales of 2.13 billion zlotys against 2.26 billion in the same period of 1995.

It exports coal and coke mainly to Denmark, Sweden, Finland, Germany, the Czech Republic, Austria, Ukraine and Russia. It ranks among the top three Polish exporters and among the top 20 companies in central and eastern Europe in terms of sales.
